validity.recommendation: verify against the FERC eLibrary docket CP18-37-000 directly (FederalRegister.gov is bot-walled from this seat) whether 'Puerto Libertad Expansion' (P2614, Capacity=427 MMcf/d) is the SAME physical Sierrita Compressor Expansion Project already recorded as P2615 'Sierrita Pima Expansion' (320 MMcf/d) -- if confirmed, retire/merge P2614 rather than treat it as an independent 427 MMcf/d increment stacked on top of P2615's 320
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE is solid -- the underlying construction project is real and independently documented (FERC docket CP18-37-000, a new ~15,900 hp compressor station in Pima County, AZ; approved by FERC ~Oct 1-3, 2018 per Utility Dive, 'FERC authorizes expansion of US-Mexico pipeline', https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-authorizes-expansion-of-us-mexico-pipeline/538677/, published 2018-10-03, verified). But the CAPACITY figure recorded for this row (427 MMcf/d, narrated on gem.wiki as 'increased capacity on the Sierrita Pipeline from 200 MMcf/d to 627 MMcf/d') does NOT match any primary source I could independently verify, and appears to duplicate/conflict with P2615's own (verified) figures for what looks like the SAME physical project. What I actually verified: (1) Utility Dive (real content fetched and read directly, not just the search snippet -- the default url_verifier UA gets a 403 bot-wall on this host, but a browser UA gets 200 with the full article; same false-negative class the script's docstring already documents for other bot-walled hosts) states the CP18-37 compressor project raises Sierrita from 200,846 Dth/d to 'almost 323,000 Dth/d' (~323 MMcf/d total, i.e. a ~122,000 Dth/d increment), cost ~$56 million -- the SAME $56M figure gem.wiki attributes to 'Sierrita Pima Expansion' (P2615). (2) Kinder Morgan's own SEC Form 8-K earnings exhibit for Q4 2019 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1506307/000150630720000002/kmi2019q48-kex991.htm, verified) describes a Sierrita expansion 'increas[ing] the pipeline's capacity by approximately 323,000 Dth/d to 524,000 Dth/d,' completion expected Q2 2020. (3) EIA's Today in Energy piece ({EIA}, verified) independently confirms a '0.32 Bcf/d Sierrita Pima Expansion... completed in early 2020' -- 0.32 Bcf/d = 320 MMcf/d, matching P2615's recorded Capacity almost exactly, and NOT naming any separate 'Puerto Libertad Expansion.' (4) Kinder Morgan's own FY2022 10-K ({KMI2022}, verified, page/line: 'Sierrita 35% 60 [miles] 0.52 [Bcf/d capacity]') reports Sierrita's TOTAL system capacity as of FY2022 as 0.52 Bcf/d = 520 MMcf/d -- i.e. 200 (original, confirmed via the 2018 10-K's '60 [miles] 0.20 [Bcf/d]' entry for the same asset) + 320 (Pima Expansion), with NO further increment for a separate 427 MMcf/d 'Puerto Libertad Expansion.' If a second, independent 427 MMcf/d project had actually gone into service, KMI's own reported system capacity would be far higher than 520. (5) A Mexican federal government document (SENER/CRE status report, Oct 2017, https://www.gob.mx/cms/uploads/attachment/file/265260/Estatus_Gasoductos_octubre_2017.pdf, verified) lists the ORIGINAL Sierrita line (Tucson-Sasabe, 97 km, in service Dec 2014, Sierrita Gas LLC = MGI-Mitsui-KM) at 195 mmpcd capacity with a footnote that it 'sera expandida hasta 770 mmpcd' (will be expanded up to 770 mmpcd) per CFE's requirements -- a THIRD, still different, larger PLANNED ceiling figure from Oct 2017, distinct from both 627 and the 520/524 actually realized. This confirms 'Puerto Libertad' is the name of the Sonora town where a SEPARATE, IENova/CFE-owned Mexican pipeline (Sasabe-Pto. Libertad, 'Proyecto Noroeste' Tramo I, 218 km, also in service Dec 2014) receives Sierrita's exported gas -- i.e. 'Puerto Libertad' names the downstream Mexican market/destination the US compressor expansion was built to serve, not a second, separate US-side pipeline construction project. I could NOT independently verify the '627 MMcf/d' / '427 MMcf/d increment' figures against any primary document -- the only place they surfaced was gem.wiki's own narrative and one search-tool synthesized answer that also claimed the FederalRegister.gov notice states these numbers; when I fetched that exact URL directly, it returned FederalRegister.gov's bot-wall CAPTCHA page (title-tag text only, no article body), so that synthesis could not have come from the real page and should not be trusted -- flagging this as a near-miss so nobody downstream treats it as read. Net: P2614 and P2615 both describe -- with high confidence -- the SAME physical CP18-37 compressor project (same new compressor station in Pima County AZ, same $56M cost figure, same Oct 2018 FERC approval window, same 2020 completion), but carry two different, non-additive capacity figures (427 vs 320) neither of which, if simply added to each other or to the original 200, matches KMI's own verified FY2022 total of 520 MMcf/d. This is either a duplicate row or, at minimum, a spec error on Capacity -- not a fillable REFS_ADDED. I have NOT staged a confirming ref for Capacity on this row; see the paired fills[] entry (UNRESOLVED).
